title: The crammed center of Messier 22
caption: The center of the globular cluster Messier 22, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Messier 22, NGC 6656 · constellation Sagittarius · about 10000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble image shows the crowded center of the globular cluster Messier 22. Globular clusters are ball-shaped swarms of tightly packed stars left over from the early Universe, typically 12 to 13 billion years old, which is very old given that the Universe itself is only 13.8 billion years old.

At just 10 000 light-years away, Messier 22 is one of the closest of the Milky Way's roughly 150 globular clusters. Abraham Ihle discovered it in 1665, one of the earliest globulars to be discovered. That is no surprise, since it ranks among the brightest seen from the northern hemisphere, lying in Sagittarius near the Galactic Bulge. Even so, dust and gas between us and the cluster dim its starlight.

Messier 22 has some unusual residents. Six planet-sized objects that do not orbit any star have been detected there, the cluster seems to host two black holes, and it is among just three clusters known to hold a planetary nebula, a short-lived shell of gas thrown off by a dying star.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.42 x 3.49 arcminutes) and distance (10000 light years), the frame spans roughly 9.9 × 10 light-years. Its light set out about 10,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines visible and near-infrared exposures from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys. The color assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, and Hubble's sharp view separates the crowded stars at the cluster's center.

explore: The cluster is about 70 light-years across and covers a patch of sky as large as the full Moon. The image combines visible and near-infrared exposures from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys.
alt: The crowded center of a globular cluster, densely packed with stars.
